\maketitle \begin{abstract} For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $H(n)$ denote the maximum number of vertices in a hypergraph with no isolated vertices and with no partition of size greater than $n$ in the sense of Brian and Larson. We give a self-contained lower-bound construction showing that for every fixed integer $t \ge 2$, \[ H(n) \ge \frac{H_t - 1}{\ln t}\, n \ln n - O_t(n), \] where $H_t = \sum_{j=1}^t \frac1j$ is the $t$th harmonic number. Thus $H$ may be identified with a finite multiset $\mathcal S$ of nonempty subsets of $[m]$. For $P \subseteq [m]$, define the exact-one count \[ \operatorname{ex1}_{\mathcal S}(P) := \bigl|\{ S \in \mathcal S : |S \cap P| = 1\}\bigr|, \] with multiplicities counted.
